blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Engineers write: "if feeder upgrades F1 and F2 are both funded, substation S must be rebuilt." With Booleans f1, f2 and s, which CP-SAT constraint states exactly that rule?

options.says: That is 'at least one of the three', which refuses funding none of them and allows f1 and f2 without s.
That forces all three to be funded, whatever the plan.
Right: the clause refuses only f1 = 1, f2 = 1, s = 0, which is the one combination the rule forbids.
These run the wrong way: they say a rebuilt substation needs both upgrades.

origin.section: Each Logic Constraint Allows Exactly the Assignments Its Name Says

questions.stem: A crew row must hold only in plans that fund project A and do not fund project B, with Booleans a and b. How is the row switched?

options.text: `.only_enforce_if(a, ~b)` on the row: one call with both literals
options.says: Right: several enforcement literals mean all of them, so the row holds exactly when a is true and b is false.

options.text: two copies of the row, one with `.only_enforce_if(a)`, one with `~b`
options.says: Each copy holds when its own literal is true, so the row would hold whenever either is true.

options.text: `.only_enforce_if(a - b)` on the row: one call with the difference
options.says: Enforcement takes literals, not linear expressions; a - b is an expression.

options.text: a big-M term on the row, since every call takes a single literal
options.says: `only_enforce_if` takes any number of literals; no M is needed.

origin.section: OnlyEnforceIf Switches a Linear Row On a Conjunction of Literals

questions.stem: A model maximizes NPV plus a $200k bonus, earned through a Boolean b when vegetation capex is more than $3,000k (capex in whole $k). Only one enforced row may be added for b. Which row makes the bonus honest?

options.says: This says nothing when b is true, so the solver takes the bonus with any capex, as the rebate run showed.

options.text: no row at all, since the objective always sets b to its true value
options.says: The objective pushes b toward 1 whatever the capex; nothing ties b to the spending.
That makes the bonus require low capex, the opposite of the rule.

options.text: `add(capex >= 3001).only_enforce_if(b)`, which needs more capex for b
options.says: Right: the solver wants b true, so the row enforced on b is the side it would otherwise exploit.

origin.section: Write the Side the Objective Would Exploit, or Both
